audit_findings.title: Legacy decommissioning guarantees are unbridged claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $23.8m-$39.5m of named exposure net of specified bonds; $7.4m is accrued, leaving a potentially unaccrued $16.4m-$32.1m, equal to about $0.11-$0.21 per diluted share or 4.1%-8.0% of $403m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: One-time decommissioning claims reduce the equity bridge unless already captured as cash costs in owner earnings; the current bridge deducts none of them.
audit_findings.evidence: To the extent that Maritech or Orinoco fails to satisfy decommissioning liabilities associated with any of the Orinoco Lease Liabilities or the Legacy Liabilities, we may be required to satisfy such liabilities under third party indemnity agreements and corporate guarantees that we previously provided to the U.S. Department of the Interior (“BSEE”) and other parties, respectively, for which costs may be significant.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantees and named claims are demonstrated, but ultimate liability and recovery from bonds, Orinoco, the Clarkes, or other owners remain unresolved. The filed exposure is large enough relative to the valuation to require an explicit bridge adjustment or probability-weighted scenario.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each claim to the $7.4m accrual, bond proceeds, historical owner-earnings charges, indemnification rights and expected legal costs; rerun all scenarios after deducting the probability-weighted amount not otherwise captured.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter conflicts with a material plant under construction
audit_findings.magnitude: $71.1m spent or capitalized through June 2026, comprising $62.7m of disclosed project costs and $8.4m of capitalized interest, plus $42.2m of disclosed construction and power commitments; future earnings and total remaining cost are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The project changes forecast capital expenditures, financing and share count, and eventually owner earnings and growth; a null perimeter omits those linked changes.
audit_findings.evidence: Phase 2 will include major infrastructure and equipment supporting the processing plant with mechanical completion projected by the end of 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error: the plant passed final investment decision, construction is underway, and disclosed commitments equal about 10.5% of the $403m base equity value. Direction is mixed because excluding plant earnings understates value, while excluding remaining spending, execution risk or financing overstates it.
audit_findings.action: Build a 2026-2028 project schedule covering all remaining capital expenditures, capitalized interest, partner reimbursements, financing, start-up timing and incremental owner earnings, then rerun each scenario without double-counting issued shares, cash or growth.

audit_findings.title: The selected anchor may contain a non-repeatable working-capital release
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.426m source from trade payables and accrued expenses, equal to 162.3% of the $16.9m anchor; the portion included in owner earnings is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A temporary increase in operating liabilities inflates cash-based owner earnings; capitalizing it in the anchor overstates forecast owner earnings and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Operating cash flows increased compared to the prior year primarily driven by continued strength in our offshore completion fluids and industrial calcium chloride businesses plus a strong focus on working capital management.
audit_findings.explanation: The working-capital source is demonstrated, but the record does not establish how much entered the $16.9m anchor. Because the filed source exceeds the entire anchor, even partial inclusion could materially change the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor to the cash-flow statement and normalize receivables, inventories, payables, accrued expenses and taxes using a sustainable working-capital requirement; rerun all scenarios with the normalized anchor.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest may violate the premise that interest remains inside owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.5m in 2025, equal to 26.6% of the $16.9m anchor; an additional $3.9m was capitalized in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized interest bypasses income-statement interest expense and overstates equity-level owner earnings if the corresponding project expenditure is excluded from the owner-earnings capital-expenditure deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we capitalized $ 4.5 million and $ 1.2 million of interest expense, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Capitalization is demonstrated, but omission from owner earnings is not. The 2025 amount is sufficiently large relative to the anchor to be material if Arkansas growth capital was classified outside the deduction.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $4.5m through the 2025 owner-earnings calculation and the Arkansas capital-expenditure classification; if absent, deduct it as an equity cash cost and rerun all scenarios, while separately incorporating 2026 capitalized interest in the project perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Accrued abandoned-office costs may disappear between the historical anchor and forecast cash flows
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.9m gross before lease concessions, at most about $0.039 per diluted share and 1.5% of the $403m base equity value before discounting
audit_findings.mechanism: If the noncash accrual was added back, the later facility cash payments require a one-time forecast or bridge deduction, net of concessions.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon abandonment of our former corporate office in late 2025 that is not subleased, we recorded a non-cash charge of approximately $ 9.5 million, including a $ 3.6 million impairment of the right of use asset and accrual of approximately $ 5.9 million of estimated facility management and operational costs expected to be incurred through the lease expiration in December 2027, which is included in other (income) expense, net in our consolidated statements of operations, and will be offset by concessions from the new lease during 2026 and 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting mismatch remains possible, but the filed gross amount establishes its maximum standalone scale. Even assuming no concessions and no prior owner-earnings capture, the direct reduction is less than $5.9m and does not change the valuation's no-buy conclusion at a $6.91 market price versus $2.27-$2.92 estimated value.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the $5.9m accrual was added back and document the 2026-2027 concessions; include any net payment as a dated one-time cash outflow, without capitalizing it as recurring expense.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $37.6m of FY2020 residual D&A, computed from $81.0m representing 68.3% of filed D&A
audit_findings.mechanism: Any eligible residual D&A would increase FY2020 owner earnings, but it does not affect the selected 2025 anchor, shares or equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2020 $81.0m (68.3% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: No overstatement error is demonstrated because the residual was retained as an expense. Although classification could raise FY2020 owner earnings, the valuation explicitly rejected the historical series as an anchor and used latest actual 2025 owner earnings, so correcting FY2020 alone cannot change the current valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual only if filed evidence identifies eligible non-economic D&A; rerun the historical series only if that evidence would also justify abandoning the stated 2025 latest-actual anchor rule.
